evidence.observation: 'GC2 adds the opt-in API keyword and CLI flag, packaged guidance and runnable include-backed example. Verify unchanged default output, CLI/API byte parity from an installed wheel' names no command, no Python function, no flag name and no keyword name.

'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture.' and 'Document the flag and keyword on existing CLI and Python reference pages.' never say which existing output counts as the 'ordinary review', or which reference pages are meant.

concerns.recommendation: Name the exact CLI subcommand and flag, the API function and keyword, and the existing output used as the ordinary baseline. Capture that default output as a golden file before GC2 lands, so 'unchanged default output' compares against fixed bytes rather than a later rerun.
concerns.title: The CLI command, flag, API function and keyword being extended are never named, so compatibility and parity cannot be falsified

evidence.observation: 'Use a view digest for replay. Check original root bytes and verified transitive include pins before applying evolution because evidence-only changes can preserve the view digest.' The listed view fields include no root SHA-256 or include pins, so the 'original root bytes' cannot be recovered from the view.

The host record lists 'exact view digest' but not the root SHA-256. §6 claims 'Existing evolution preview and apply perform stale-state checks.' Context: src/gnd/evolve/service.py:1715 only compares proposal.expected_model_sha256 against the current root bytes. A host that computes that value after a concurrent round, rather than taking it from the view, passes the check while acting on a stale view, and can then add a duplicate the view never showed.

concerns.recommendation: Have the projection emit, or the API return beside it, the root SHA-256 and the include pins it was rendered from. Require the host to copy that value into expected_model_sha256 and to record it. Add a GC2 test: render the view, add a fact type non-additively elsewhere, then show that a proposal built from the old view is refused as stale.
concerns.title: The view digest is not tied to the root bytes that evolve's stale-state check compares

evidence.observation: 'Issue 295 asks for compact prompt context' yet the only check is 'Compare compact versus ordinary review bytes on the same populated schema fixture.' No comparison outcome is stated as a pass or a fail.

'Measure actual UTF-8 bytes and confine comparisons to the measured fixture.' and 'Record measured sizes and any limitations.' only record a number. A projection larger than the ordinary output would still satisfy this wording.

concerns.recommendation: State a falsifiable criterion on the named fixture, at minimum compact bytes strictly below ordinary bytes, ideally a ratio. Assert it in the GC1 test so that a regression in size fails the build.
concerns.title: Compactness, the issue's headline requirement, has no pass criterion

evidence.observation: 'a first miss followed by successful lookup of an included fact via its role players, and ambiguous deferral.' Neither 'miss' nor 'ambiguous' is defined. The plan excludes search (§7) and gives search to the host (§3), so the example's miss is staged by the script itself.

'A subset miss requires broader investigation or deferral before asserting novelty. The agent may choose a different search route each round.' No check shows that the rule is followed, or that breaking it is detected.

concerns.recommendation: Define ambiguity: for example, two or more fact types with the same ordered role players and no reading match. Make the example take its lookup result from the CLI or API output bytes, not from fixture constants. Assert the negatives: no evolve apply after a deferral, and no novel add after a subset miss that was never broadened.
concerns.title: The retry and deferral evidence is a scripted example with no defined ambiguity and no negative assertions

evidence.observation: 'Version 1 is canonical UTF-8 JSON with a trailing newline.' and 'Use a view digest for replay.' name no encoder. Nor do they say whether the digest covers the trailing newline, or whether it is embedded in the bytes it hashes. Context: the repo already has src/gnd/artifacts.py:174 canonical_json_bytes (with an exact_numbers option), src/gnd/discover/output.py:35 canonical_bytes and src/gnd/export/ilp_amie.py:224 canonical_bytes.

concerns.recommendation: Name the encoder to reuse (artifacts.canonical_json_bytes) and its options. Define the digest as SHA-256 over the exact emitted bytes, newline included, and keep it outside those bytes. Pin the digest of one fixture in a test.
concerns.title: Neither the canonical encoder nor the bytes the view digest covers is defined

evidence.observation: 'Version 1' is asserted, but no schema_version or kind field and no packaged JSON Schema is planned. Context: other outputs ship beside the code as files such as src/gnd/diff.schema.json and src/gnd/discover.schema.json. §5 documents only 'the flag and keyword'.

concerns.recommendation: Emit schema_version and kind in the bytes and ship a packaged schema for the projection. Validate GC1 fixtures against it, so a host can detect a version 2 and refuse it.
concerns.title: The output carries no version field and has no schema file

evidence.observation: 'Preserve meaningful order and use deterministic ordering elsewhere.' lists neither the meaningful orders nor the sort key. 'deterministic bytes' tests only that repeat runs agree; it cannot show that a cosmetic YAML or include reordering leaves the bytes unchanged.

concerns.recommendation: List the meaningful orders (for example role order and reading order) and the sort key used elsewhere (for example the ID by code point). Add permutation tests: reorder fact types and includes in the source and expect identical bytes; swap the role order and expect different bytes.
concerns.title: Ordering rules are not specified, so the digest may change on cosmetic edits

evidence.observation: 'GND supplies a complete read-only inventory of the resolved model.' but only 'registered constraint signatures' are exposed. Nothing says what happens to an unregistered or extension constraint kind, an objectified fact type or a value constraint.
'empty models, unresolved includes' are listed as tests without an expected outcome, such as an exit code or whether partial output is allowed.

concerns.recommendation: Fail closed: refuse to render, with a named exit, any construct the projection cannot represent, and any unresolved include. Alternatively emit an explicit omission marker. Add a test with an unregistered constraint kind.
concerns.title: A 'complete inventory' can silently drop unregistered constructs, and unresolved-include behaviour is not specified

evidence.observation: 'Check the role-specific occurrence before reusing a fact.' and 'Ordered role-player signatures preserve direction.' Context: the guide's shape report already 'lists existing fact types over the same role players' (unattended-growth.md:57-58). A reversed-direction or ring fact type shares the same players.

concerns.recommendation: Define 'role-specific occurrence'. Add a GC2 negative case: a fact type with the same players in reversed roles, and a ring fact type, where the host must not reuse the existing ID.
concerns.title: No test shows that a fact with the same players in reversed roles is not reused

evidence.observation: 'The host records actual prompt scope, full or partial status, exact view digest, queries, inspected IDs, chosen action and source occurrence.' gives no location or format, and GC2 verification never checks the record. Context: the guide already logs rounds through 'gnd evolve summary ... --record D' (unattended-growth.md:60).

concerns.recommendation: Say whether these fields extend the round-summary schema, which is a compatibility change and needs a version bump, or live in a separate host log. Have the GC2 example assert that the fields are present.
concerns.title: The host record's location, format and compatibility are unspecified and nothing verifies it

evidence.observation: 'Expose object IDs and reference modes, fact IDs' and 'Loader checks protect composed ID identity' rely on the loader, but only one 'direct reuse' is checked. Nothing asserts that every emitted ID, including IDs from included files, is the form evolve accepts as an existing ID.

concerns.recommendation: In GC1, assert that every emitted ID resolves through ModelIndex. In GC2, reuse one root element and one included element through evolve preview.
concerns.title: No test checks that emitted IDs round-trip as evolve reuse targets

response.summary: The two-phase scope is sound: one renderer behind both surfaces, evidence excluded, the host left to choose its own search. But several product obligations cannot be implemented or falsified as written. The plan never names the CLI command, API function, flag or keyword it extends, so 'unchanged default output' and the compact-versus-ordinary comparison have no fixed baseline. The view digest is recorded without the root SHA-256 it was rendered from, so the existing compare-and-swap on expected_model_sha256 does not protect a host that works from a stale view. Compactness has no pass criterion. The retry and deferral evidence is a scripted example with no definition of ambiguity and no negative assertions. Smaller risks to schema identity and compatibility: an unnamed canonical encoder, no version field or schema file, an ordering rule that is not specified, silent omission of unregistered constructs, and no test that a reversed-direction fact is not reused.
